Orientation · both tracks

One dataset, read two honest ways

This report runs on two parallel tracks of equal weight. Read either on its own, or use the All · Method · Leads switch at the top to bring one into focus.

Track A — What the method delivers

Rigor you can audit

A corrected, statistically defensible pipeline. Its most important output is an honest null: at n = 2 technical replicates, nothing survives multiple-testing correction — and the pipeline is built to say so out loud.

  • Three fold-change bugs found in the legacy script, then fixed
  • limma + MinProb, QC that surfaces its own limitations
  • The enrichment background trap, deliberately avoided
  • Config-driven, schema-validated, seed-fixed, sha256-frozen
Track B — Biological leads to follow up

Hypotheses, clearly labelled

The same data, mined for structure worth a second experiment. Every item here is hypothesis-generating only — a ranked to-do list for when biological replicates exist, never a claim of significance.

  • Top candidate proteins by ranked p-value
  • Cytoskeletal, chaperone & ribosomal interaction hubs
  • Suggestive pathway themes, all sub-threshold
  • 10 on/off + 606 single-condition proteins as candidate pools

The caveat ribbon at the top stays visible on every screen of this document. It is not decoration — it is the single most important sentence in the report.

02
Framing spine · both tracks

The experiment, and its hard ceiling

A SILAC label-free comparison in mouse: testosterone-treated material carries the Heavy label, vehicle control the Light. Two runs per condition — technical replicates of one biological sample, not a population.

The four measured channels are 31578, 31580 (Light / control) and 31579, 31581 (Heavy / treated). Because both replicates re-measure the same biological material, their p-values describe “is this ratio reproducible on this instrument,” not “does testosterone change this protein in the population.” That distinction is the governing constraint of the entire analysis, and it is why the significance line is never reached.

A correction worth flagging. The original design document assumed a human system (taxid 9606). Inspection of the committed data showed otherwise: 99.7% of gene symbols are title-case MGI nomenclature (Lama1, Sptan1, Cryab), and H2-K1 is a mouse MHC class-I gene. The organism was corrected to Mus musculus, taxid 10090, and every organism-specific step — STRING, g:Profiler, Enrichr libraries — was re-pointed to mouse. Human parameters would have returned meaningless mappings.

03
Track A — Method

Three ways to average a ratio wrong

The legacy 88-line script produced UP / DOWN calls — with three correctness bugs baked into the fold-change logic. The first one changes the answer, not just the rounding.

Bug 1 — arithmetic mean of ratios, then log. SILAC ratios are multiplicative; their correct centre is the geometric mean (equivalently, the mean of the log₂ ratios). Averaging the raw ratios first systematically inflates apparent up-regulation. The worked example below is the whole bug in two numbers.

Worked example — one protein, two runsBug 1 · arithmetic vs geometric mean
Run 1 · H/L ratio
2.0×
twofold up in run 1
Run 2 · H/L ratio
0.5×
twofold down in run 2
Legacy · arithmetic mean → log₂
(2.0 + 0.5) / 2 = 1.25
log₂(1.25) = +0.32  → reads “UP” · WRONG
Correct · geometric mean = mean of log₂
√(2.0 × 0.5) = 1.00
log₂(1.00) = 0.00  → no change · CORRECT

Bug 2 — asymmetric thresholds on the log₂ scale. “UP” fired at ratio ≥ 1.5 (log₂ = +0.585) while “DOWN” required ratio ≤ 0.5 (log₂ = −1.0). A protein had to rise only 1.5× to be called up, but fall a full 2× to be called down. The symmetric partner of a 1.5× cut is 1/1.5 = 0.667 (log₂ = −0.585) — so the classifier was quietly biased against detecting down-regulation.

Bug 3 — inf / NaN propagation. Ratios were computed for every row before the zero/missing filter, so a zero Light denominator produced inf, and log₂(0) produced −inf. These non-finite values were excluded from the UP/DOWN call but survived in the saved artifact, ready to break any downstream consumer that did not re-filter.

And a silent fourth. The inner join on accession kept only proteins seen in both sheets — discarding the on/off proteins that are often the strongest biological signal, with no log. Corrected in the next section.

Track A — Method

Rebuilt in log-space, nothing dropped

A fresh proteomics_de/ module reproduces the corrected logic and leaves the legacy script frozen and untouched — a benchmark to diff against.

The three arithmetic bugs are fixed at the source: fold changes are the mean of log2_rep1 and log2_rep2, the regulation cutoff is symmetric at |log₂FC| ≥ 0.585, and non-finite values never reach the saved table. Just as important, the merge no longer silently loses data: the 606 single-condition and 10 on/off proteins the inner join used to drop are now carried into their own audited CSVs as separate candidate pools (returned to in Track B). Of the 1,948 both-condition proteins, 715 clear the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.585 effect-size gate — 206 up, 509 down — but that is an effect-size list, not yet a significance claim. That comes next.

05
Track A — Method

Quality control that surfaces bad news

Good QC is not a green checklist — it is the part of the pipeline allowed to disagree with you. Two checks return WARN, and the report keeps them in view rather than tuning them away.

0.27
Fold-change replicate r
WARN · threshold 0.50
−0.28
Mean log₂FC (centering)
WARN · tolerance 0.10
0.86 / 0.84
Raw replicate r
control / treated intensities
56.3%
Fold-change sign agreement
889 / 1,578 proteins

The honest limitation, surfaced. Raw intensities reproduce well between runs (Pearson r = 0.86 control, 0.84 treated). But the fold-change — a difference of two large, similar numbers — is noisy: replicate r = 0.27, below the 0.50 gate, so the check returns WARN. Subtracting two near-equal quantities amplifies small wobbles, so per-protein up/down calls at n = 2 are not individually trustworthy. This is not a failure to hide; it is precisely the on-paper justification for limma, which borrows information across all ~1,938 proteins to stabilise each estimate when single-protein replicates cannot.

The centering check likewise returns WARN (mean log₂FC = −0.28 against a ±0.10 tolerance) and writes a centered copy for inspection, without overriding the “no normalization” rule that the recipe calls for. Per-sample intensity distributions are near-identical (medians 27.4–27.8 log₂), which is the basis for not adding a cross-sample normalization step; and most “missingness” is structural — proteins genuinely absent from one condition — rather than random dropout.

06
Track A — Method

limma + MinProb, and the line nothing reaches

The statistically defensible core, per Peng et al. 2024: no extra normalization, MinProb imputation for left-censored missingness, and a limma moderated t-test with empirical-Bayes shrinkage.

1,938
Proteins tested
both-condition; on/off excluded
0
Pass FDR < 0.05
min adj.p = 0.305
63
At raw p < 0.05
nominal only
0.116
Min adj.p, trend/robust
still > 0.05
1.0000
corr(limma, pipeline log₂FC)
contrast wired correctly

With two values per group, a per-protein t-test has essentially no power and a wildly unstable variance estimate. limma’s empirical Bayes shrinks each protein’s variance toward a global trend — the one thing that makes inference possible at small n. It runs cleanly here, and the result is unambiguous: 0 of 1,938 proteins reach FDR < 0.05, with the smallest adjusted p-value at 0.305. The field-standard trend + robust refinement sharpens the extremes — the smallest adjusted p falls to 0.116 — but still crosses nothing. Critically, corr(limma log₂FC, pipeline log₂FC) = 1.0000: the contrast is wired correctly, so the null is a real property of the data at n = 2, not a plumbing error. The volcano therefore draws the raw p = 0.05 line for orientation only — there is no FDR line to draw, because nothing crosses it.

07
Track A — Method

The background that manufactures a story

The most instructive result in the whole report is a trap avoided. Choose the wrong enrichment background and a null dataset produces a confident pathway narrative.

The background-inflation trap

Over-representation asks whether your gene list is enriched relative to a background. The right background is the detected proteome — the 2,554 proteins that could have been seen. The naive background is the whole genome.

0
terms significant · correct custom background
(2,554 detected proteins · g:SCS-corrected)
196
“significant” terms · naive whole-genome background
(top: GO:CC “cytoplasm”, p ≈ 1.9 × 10⁻²³)

Same UP gene list, same tool. The 196-term story is an artifact of comparing detected proteins to the whole genome rather than to what could have been detected. The pipeline uses the detected-proteome background and therefore does not fall into it — the honest answer at n = 2 is that no enrichment survives correction.

Both enrichment tests agree with the per-protein null and are reported as separate statistical tests from it — never conflated. g:Profiler ORA against the custom background returns 0 terms in either direction (best corrected p ≈ 0.70). Preranked GSEA over 568 mouse gene sets returns 0 at FDR < 0.05 (minimum FDR q = 0.125). The sub-threshold leads that do exist are carried into Track B, labelled for exactly what they are.

08
Track A — Method

Analyses that know when to switch off

Every multivariate method registers a minimum sample count. A dispatcher runs only those whose requirement is met and logs the rest — so PCA and clustering appear here strictly as QC, not as biology.

At n = 4 the sample covariance matrix is rank-deficient: exactly three principal components exist by construction, eigenvalues are biased, and PC1 can be driven by a single sample. So PCA and hierarchical clustering run in QC-only mode — a sanity check that technical replicate pairs sit near each other — below the trustworthy gate of n ≥ 6. Heavier methods are skipped outright, each with its reason recorded in a machine-readable registry.

AnalysisNeedsHaveStatusWhy
PCA64QC onlyRank-deficient covariance; eigenvalues biased; PC1 can be one sample.
Hierarchical clustering64QC onlyNo bootstrap support possible; dendrogram topology not stable.
WGCNA154SkipCo-expression modules need ≥15 (ideally ≥20) samples for stable topology.
UMAP / t-SNE244SkipEmbeddings need dozens of samples to be stable.
mixOmics sPLS-DA204SkipMultivariate CV needs samples ≫ classes.
VAE / GNN10004SkipThousands of samples required to train without overfitting.
09
Track A — Method

Reproducible by construction

A single declarative config.yaml is the source of truth for design, thresholds and file contracts; adversarial schema validation checks the frozen outputs against it.

Five committed CSV contracts are validated with pandera schemas built by inspecting the real data, not an idealised spec — they accommodate O/P/Q-prefixed UniProt accessions, semicolon-joined protein groups, NaN gene names, and one narrowly-scoped documented data quirk, while still rejecting anything genuinely malformed. The last run passed 5 / 5 files, with cross-file arithmetic checked too: 1,948 − 10 = 1,938 and 1,948 + 606 = 2,554. MinProb is stochastic, so its seed is fixed (42); package versions are pinned; and outputs are frozen — the reproducibility layer never edits the pipeline it describes.

Track B — Leads

Patterns in the top forty

Row-standardized log₂ intensities for the 40 proteins with the smallest raw p-values, clustered by protein. A view for the eye to find structure — not a significance display.

Selection is by smallest raw p-value, deliberately — not by largest |log₂FC| — so the panel reflects the ranked evidence rather than the loudest effect sizes. Nine up, twenty-four down among the forty.

12
Track B — Leads

Where the candidates connect

A STRING v12.0 network seeded by the 715 regulated proteins. Structure here reflects STRING’s curated evidence, not significance in this dataset — but the hubs cluster into readable themes.

Of 715 seeds, 694 (97.1%) mapped to a STRING identifier, giving a 694-node / 5,963-edge network across 57 communities; the largest connected component (645 nodes) is drawn. The highest-degree hubs read as three familiar programmes — cytoskeletal (Actb), chaperone (Hsp90aa1, Cct7, Tcp1), and ribosomal / translational (Rps3, Rps20, Rpsa) — exactly the kind of coherent scaffold worth a hypothesis, and exactly the kind that a curated database will surface whether or not this experiment had the power to confirm it.

13
Track B — Leads

Themes worth a second experiment

The strongest sub-threshold signals from ORA and GSEA. Every one of these is not significant — listed as directions to probe, never as findings.

On the UP side, the best (still non-significant) ORA lead is dephosphorylation (GO:BP, corrected p ≈ 0.70, 11 genes including Ppp2ca, Ppp1cc, Ppp1ca), alongside mRNA-splicing Reactome terms that share genes Prosc and Tpd52l2. Preranked GSEA’s leading themes lean toward secretion and protein-transport regulation on the up side (top NES: positive regulation of secretion by cell) and mitotic cell-cycle / chromosome-organization on the down side — 40 terms clear a nominal p < 0.05 but none clear FDR (minimum q = 0.125). The UpSet panel shows where the top ORA leads share genes; by construction up- and down-side terms never overlap, so it reads as two disjoint clusters rather than a display error.

14
Track B — Leads

Two candidate pools the old join threw away

The proteins that are present in one arm and absent in the other are often the most interesting — and were exactly what the legacy inner join discarded without a log.

On / off · 10 proteins

All-or-nothing signals

Detected in one condition and genuinely zero in the other — the most dramatic candidate switches. Too few, and too extreme, to test with limma (a whole condition would have to be imputed), so they are kept as a labelled pool rather than forced through a model.

Single-condition · 606 proteins

Present in only one arm

Identified in control-only or treated-only, with no cross-condition ratio to compute. Excluded from limma by design — imputing an entire missing condition manufactures data — but retained as a rich, separate follow-up pool once biological replicates make their presence/absence pattern testable.

Together these two pools account for the gap between the 1,938 tested and the 2,554 detected. Nothing is deleted silently; everything is filed where it can be picked up again.

15
Forward path · both tracks

What unlocks with biological replicates

The ceiling here is replication, not architecture. Because every analysis is gated on a sample count and every design choice lives in the sample sheet, growing the study is a config change, not a rewrite.

Adding biological replicates means appending rows to sample_sheet.tsv (new sample IDs, replicate index 3, 4, …); the design matrix model.matrix(~group) regenerates automatically, and the three-file contract is replicate-count-agnostic by construction. At that point the p-values graduate from “technical reproducibility” to “population-level biological significance” — and the caveat ribbon comes off. Each gated analysis switches itself on as its sample threshold is met:

  • n ≥ 6
    Real PCA & bootstrapped clustering

    Full-rank covariance; stable dendrogram topology; genuine biological-variance FDR power.

  • n ≥ 15–20
    WGCNA co-expression modules

    Correlation networks become biologically meaningful; mixOmics sPLS-DA becomes viable.

  • dozens+
    UMAP / t-SNE sample structure

    Low-dimensional embeddings stabilise; sample-level structure becomes interpretable.

  • config
    No code rewrite required

    The dispatcher turns each method on automatically once its min_samples gate is satisfied.

The manual step

QIAGEN IPA is a human-run tool. The pipeline emits ipa_input.csv (all 715 regulated proteins) and a header-only ipa_input_significant.csv (0 significant, by design). Uploading to IPA and running Core / Pathway / Upstream-Regulator analyses is a licensed, Salesforce-hosted step that only a person can perform — no code can close that loop, and this report does not pretend to.

A null result, honestly kept.

The deliverable is not a list of significant proteins — there are none. It is a corrected, reproducible, self-auditing pipeline, a ranked set of hypotheses filed for the day biological replicates arrive, and a documented refusal to manufacture a story the data cannot support. At n = 2, that is the most useful thing the analysis can be.
